title: Ranking
description: Represent a ranked list of items related to a query, such as search results, retrieved passages, recommendations or near-duplicate matches.

producer.description: The creator (model, tool or author) of this ranking.

query.description: The text of the query, if there was one. Omitted when there was no text query (e.g. near-duplicates of a given image, or recommendations for a user).

collection.description: The name of the set the ranked items were drawn from, such as a search index, document collection or product catalogue (e.g., 'lease-agreements').

score_explanation.description: Defines the meaning of the 'score' field.

total_candidates.description: The number of candidates considered before the list was cut down to 'results'. Must not be less than the number of results, or than any result's rank.

results.description: The ranked items. Can be empty if nothing matched.

rank.description: The position of this item in the full ranking, where 1 is the best match. Tied items share a rank, and gaps are allowed (e.g. after a tie, or when results are filtered or paginated). The order of the items is given by 'rank', not by their order in the array.

id.description: An identifier for the item, such as a document id within 'collection' or a URI that resolves to it. Must be unique within 'results'.

title.description: A human-readable name for the item.

text.description: An excerpt of the item's text, such as a search snippet or a retrieved passage. May be truncated; 'id' identifies the full item.

score.description: A normalized score for this item (-1.0 to 1.0). Higher values indicate greater relevance or similarity. Depending on the use case, this may represent a probability of relevance (0 to 1) or a signed similarity such as cosine similarity (-1 to 1). Use score_explanation to clarify.

attributes.description: Arbitrary metadata for this item (e.g. a native score or distance, or the matched offset within a recording). Flat key-value pairs.
Arbitrary metadata relevant to this ranking.
